children.translated_text: Adorned with luster like conch-shells, milk, lotus-stalks, and white lotuses, with smiling garlands, with golden clouds of <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) incense, with waving banners,
resplendent with praiseworthy relics of the finest quality, resembling mountains,
I pay homage to that sage whose feet are rubbed by the crowns of gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Yakṣas</s>.

body.translated_text: May the true <s>Dharma</s> be victorious! Thus spoke the <s>bhikṣā</s> (nun) <s>Śrutasomā</s>.

body.text: asti karma alpāyuḥsaṃvartanīyam | asti karma alpāyuḥsaṃvartanīyamiti karmagatiryathānyāyaṃ vistareṇa vibhaktāḥ | daśānuśaṃsāḥ pravrajyāraṇyakatve bhaikṣyacaryāyām | daśa vaiśāradyānīti | sarve kāmaguṇā yathānyāyaṃ yuktāḥ | daśānuśaṃsāstathāgatacaityāñjalikarmagandhapuṣpacchatrāṇām | kathaṃ daśānuśaṃsāḥ? nanu bhagavatā sūtramuktamekottarike - yāvanto bhikṣavaḥ sattvā apadā vā dvipadā vā catuṣpadā vā bahupadā vā, tathāgatasteṣāṃ sattvānāmagrata ākhyāyate yadidamarhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ iti vistaraḥ | gāthā coktā -
body.translated_text: There is <s>karma</s> (action) that conduces to a short lifespan. There is <s>karma</s> that conduces to a short lifespan — thus the course of <s>karma</s> has been classified in detail according to proper method. There are ten advantages of going forth into homelessness (<s>pravrajyā</s>), of forest-dwelling (<s>āraṇyakatva</s>), and of the practice of begging for alms (<s>bhaikṣyacaryā</s>). There are ten kinds of fearlessness (<s>vaiśāradya</s>). All objects of sensory desire (<s>kāmaguṇa</s>) are rightly explained. There are ten benefits of [offering] salutations with joined palms, incense, flowers, and parasols to the <s>stūpas</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. How are there ten benefits? Indeed, the Blessed One spoke this <s>sūtra</s> in the <s>Ekottarika</s> (Numerical Discourses): 'Monks, however many beings there are — whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed — the <s>Tathāgata</s> is declared foremost among those beings, namely, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>)' — thus in detail. And a verse was spoken:

body.text:
evamacintiyo buddho buddhadharme 'pyacintiyaḥ |
yadi dharmo nvacintyo buddho 'pyacintyo
acintyaprasannasya vipāko 'pi acintiyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus inconceivable is the <s>Buddha</s>; the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddha</s> is also inconceivable; / if the <s>Dharma</s> is indeed inconceivable, the <s>Buddha</s> too is inconceivable; / and the fruit of faith in the inconceivable is also inconceivable.

body.text: kathaṃ daśa guṇāḥ puṣpacchatrādīnām? ucyate | evametadyathāsūtramuktam, tathaiva tannānyathā | ye buddhe śraddadhanti, dharme cāpi, saṃghe ca pratipannāḥ, teṣāmacintyaprasannasya vipāko 'pyacintyaḥ | ye tu mithyādarśanopahatacittāḥ, yathā - buddhasya parinirvṛtasya stūpe dattasya phalaṃ kutaḥ? yasmānnāsti pratigrāha iti, teṣāṃ viparītadṛṣṭīnām | bhagavānāha - deśeme guṇāśchatrādīnām | anenāpi tāvatsukhena puṇyāni kurvantu | tatteṣāṃ bhaviṣyati dīrgharātraṃ hitāya sukhāya | api ca sarve 'pi guṇā eteṣvevāntargatāḥ ucyante | kathaṃ punarbhagavati kṛtaḥ prasādo 'cintya iti? ucyate | yathā atraiva karmavibhaṅge uktam, evamanyeṣu sūtrānteṣu | api tu mandabuddhīnāmarthāya punaruktaṃ kriyate | yathā karṇesumanaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ sthavirāṇām -
body.translated_text: How are there ten qualities of flowers, parasols, and the like? It is said: It is just so, as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>, and not otherwise. For those who have faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, and who have entered into the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s> — for them, the fruit of faith in the inconceivable is also inconceivable. But for those whose minds are corrupted by wrong views — such as [those who say]: 'What fruit could there be from something given at the <s>stūpa</s> of the <s>Buddha</s> who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>? Since there is no recipient' — for those of perverted views, the Blessed One said: 'I shall teach the qualities of parasols and the like. By this means at least, let them create merit with ease. That will be for their benefit and happiness for a long time.' Moreover, all these qualities are said to be included within these very [offerings]. How then is faith directed toward the Blessed One said to be inconceivable? It is said: Just as stated here in this very <s>Karmavibhaṅga</s>, so too in other <s>sūtras</s>. But for the sake of those of dull intellect, this is stated again. As in the case of the elders <s>Karṇasumanas</s> and others —
By the offering of a single flower, eighty <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) [of merit];

children.translated_text: ) the divine son exercises sovereignty — seven times among the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, seven times among the <s>Sukhita</s> (Tuṣita) gods, and seven times among the <s>Yāma</s> gods he exercises sovereignty. He exercises sovereignty over thirty-six <s>Indra</s>-kingships. He rules among the gods of seventy-two <s>Mahārājika</s> realms. He exercises sovereignty over <s>koṭi</s>-<s>koṭis</s> of <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) kingdoms. If not sovereignty, this is the fruit of a single moment of faith. Moreover, one even becomes a <s>Sarvaśrāvakabuddha</s>. Just as <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> <s>Buddha</s> attained <s>Buddhahood</s> through the offering of a garland of lamps. This too is unbelievable for the faithless. Such are the actions that the world does not believe in. For those faithless ones of inferior aspiration, the Blessed One said: 'These are the ten virtues of worshipping a <s>caitya</s> (sacred shrine).' The details [are extensive]. But the <s>Buddha</s>'s greatness among those endowed with virtues is not [stated] only in the <s>Agratāsūtra</s>. As stated in the <s>Brāhmaṇasūtra</s>: 'I am the foremost, the best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in the world' — thus the <s>sūtra</s> should be applied. And just as the Blessed One went to the hermitage for the purpose of disciplining <s>Koṭu</s> the great sage and <s>Śela</s> the ascetic, and was invited to a meal by those two, the Blessed One, having known [this], uttered this <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterance):

body.translated_text: this is unbelievable. Thus the fruit is inconceivable. Likewise, for <s>Aśoka</s> and others, through the gift of a handful of dust, the attainment of universal sovereignty (<s>cakravartirājya</s>) and the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>) — this is inconceivable and unbelievable. And likewise, for <s>Aniruddha</s> and others, through the gift of a single alms-meal (<s>piṇḍapāta</s>), universal sovereignty was attained, seven divine kingships, and in the final existence, <s>Arhatship</s> was obtained. Many such [examples] could be recounted. Moreover, by a single inconceivable [act of faith], everything is encompassed. As the Blessed One stated in the <s>Abhidharma</s>, in the <s>Bālakāṇḍasūtra</s> — the fruit of a single moment of faith (<s>ekacittaprasāda</s>) has been described: 'If, <s>Ānanda</s>, while transmigrating in <s>saṃsāra</s>, by the fruit of a single moment of faith, seven times in the <s>Paranirmita</s>-

children.translated_text: The <s>Agnihotra</s> is the foremost of the <s>Vedas</s>; the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is foremost among meters;

children.text: rājā mukhaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ nadīnāṃ sāgaro mukham ||
children.translated_text: the king is foremost among humans; the ocean is foremost among rivers.
The sun is foremost among the stars and foremost among those that shine;
for those who desire merit and strive, the <s>Sambuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One) is foremost.

body.text: etaddarśayati bhagavān | yathā sarveṣāṃ yajñānāṃ jāyamānānāmagnihotraṃ mukham | vedānāṃ gāyatrī mukham | sarveṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ rājā mukham | nadīnāṃ sāgaraḥ śreṣṭhaḥ | nakṣatrāṇāṃ candramā agryaḥ | tapatāmādityaḥ pradhānaḥ sāhasrāṇāṃ lokadhātūnāmavabhāsayati | evaṃ yaścintayati - asminnekapuruṣe dattaṃ mahāphalamiti | bhagavānāha - saṃbuddho dakṣiṇeyānāmagrya iti | anenāpi kāraṇena bhagavānagrya | etatsūtramapyāgame brāhmaṇanipāte vistareṇa pratyavagantavyam | yathā ca bhagavatā etadagre dakṣiṇāvibhaṅge sūtra uktam - etadagramānanda pratipudgalikānāṃ dakṣiṇīyānāṃ yadidaṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ | evamagryatā bhagavato vaktavyā | yathā ca mahāsamājīye parinirvāṇādisūtreṣu dvādaśayojaniko devānāṃ saṃnipātaḥ | yathā mahāprātihārye 'kaniṣṭhikādibhirdevaiḥ pūjitaḥ | mahāprātihāryaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā anekāni tīrthakaraśatāni pravrajitāni | yathā ca tāpasā urubilvākāśyapaprabhṛtayaḥ pravrajitāḥ | parivrājakāśca śāriputramaudgalyāyanaprabhṛtayaḥ pravrajitāḥ | brāhmaṇāaśca brahmāyu(pūraśāyino) vasiṣṭhabhāradvājaprabhṛtayo 'bhiprasannāḥ | tathā rājānaḥ prasenajidbimbasāraprabhṛtayaḥ, gṛhapatayaḥ anāthapiṇḍadaghoṣilaprabhṛtayaḥ | evaṃ devānāṃ ye 'gryā manuṣyāṇāṃ ca, te 'bhiprasannā bhagavati | anenāpi kāraṇena bhagavān agryaḥ | api ca yathaikottarikāgratāsūtra uktam - agradharmasamanvāgato devabhūtamanuṣyāgryaḥ prāptaḥ pramoditaḥ | etaduktaṃ bhavati - nirvāṇagāmī dharmo 'dhigataḥ | tenaḥ kāraṇenāgryaḥ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ pūrvamapi bodhisattvabhūtaṃ devā upasaṃkrāntāḥ | yathā govindasūtre, śatavarge ca tāpasasūtre indra upasaṃkrāntaḥ | nanu tadā agradharmasamanvāgataḥ, sāṃprataṃ nirvāṇagāmī mārgo 'dhigataḥ | tenāgryaḥ | evamapi deśitā dharmāḥ | kecidāhuḥ - (

The <s>Buddha</s> has entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final cessation) and attained <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). Whatever is offered at his <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary shrine) or to his image — incense, flowers, and the like — who receives it? When the <s>Buddha</s> is said to have entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, this statement is faithless, or even worse than sinful, for those to whom the established doctrine of the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching is not known. This <s>Dharma</s> that the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) teaches — this is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body. And that endures today. When that disappears, the <s>Buddha</s> will have entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. As long as the <s>Dharma</s> endures, so long the <s>Buddha</s> does not enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? The <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body) is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s true body in the ultimate sense. Through that <s>Dharma</s> when taught, the fruit of <s>srotāpatti</s> (stream-entry) will be attained, the fruit of <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returning), the fruit of <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returning), and <s>arhattva</s> (arhatship). And for this purpose is our going forth into homelessness — for the sake of attaining the fruits. The <s>Buddha</s> endures; the fruits will be attained. He has not entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Otherwise, this fault would arise [that attainment is impossible]. But for us even now the fruits are being attained. For those who have exerted effort, nothing is difficult. While the <s>Buddha</s> endures, all this that must be done is accomplished. By this reason too it should be known that the <s>Tathāgata</s> has the <s>Dharma</s> as his body. As stated in the <s>Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra</s>: 'It may be, <s>Ānanda</s>, that you think: the <s>Bhagavān</s> has entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; henceforth there is no teacher. It should not be viewed thus. Henceforth, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>sūtrānta</s> (scripture) is your teacher.' Thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave the <s>sūtra</s> (discourses), <s>abhidharma</s> (higher teaching), and <s>vinaya</s> (discipline). Henceforth this is the <s>Buddha</s>. This he demonstrates. <s>Bhagavān</s> — likewise, nothing is accomplished by the body born of mother and father. This he demonstrates: 'When I dwelled at home in the household life, at that time no <s>Dharma</s> was realized by me. Therefore the body born of mother and father is not the <s>Buddha</s>. But when I, at the age of twenty-nine, left the household, those who seek the <s>Dharma</s> through suffering were amazed by the practice of austerities (<s>duṣkaracaryā</s>). Yet no <s>Dharma</s> was attained by me through suffering. As stated in the <s>Romaharṣaṇīya Sūtra</s>, so it should be understood. For six years austerities were practiced. Yet no <s>Dharma</s> was attained thereby. Afterwards, having eaten food and having gained bodily strength, seated at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree on the full-moon fifteenth day of the month of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, I attained unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Having gone to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, the Wheel of <s>Dharma</s> was set in motion. Through that <s>Dharma</s>, the attainment of fruits is accomplished. And that... By this reason too, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> have the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body). As the reading in the <s>Vinaya</s> [states]: the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s maternal aunt addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> — 'May the venerable <s>Bhagavān</s> live long...' But the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '... You should not address me thus, <s>Gautamī</s>.' She said: 'Then how should the <s>Bhagavān</s> be addressed?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Thus should it be said: May the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s> endure for a long time!' This demonstrates: there is no fulfillment through my body born of mother and father. Therefore, may my <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body) endure for a long time. The thousands of austerities I performed in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) — all those were exceedingly for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>. By this reason too, that which is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body... In the <s>Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra</s> it is stated: '<s>Ānanda</s>, the gods have come, bearing divine sandalwood powder, divine <s>Māndārava</s> flowers, divine... <s>Ānanda</s>, it is not thus that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is honored, respected, revered, or worshipped. But rather, <s>Ānanda</s>, whoever dwells diligently in my teaching... practices the <s>Dharma</s> and upholds the <s>Dharma</s> — by that person am I honored, respected, revered, and worshipped.' This he demonstrates. [In the time of] <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, monks and nuns, male and female lay-followers — they performed worship of the bodily relics, but did not uphold the <s>Dharma</s>. Eventually the <s>Dharma</s> disappeared. Even if one were to do likewise... [the <s>Dharma</s>] should be honored. This is my body. This he demonstrates —
[Reference: KVU, Vaidya 215]

children.text: ) mayi parinirvṛte yatkartavyam | dharmaṃ satkariṣyata evoktam | dharmakāyāsta(thāgatāḥ) | mahāparinivāṇe āryānandaḥ pṛcchati - kathamasmābhirbhagavati parinirvṛte bhagavaccharīrapratipattiḥ kāryā? bhagavānāha - alpotsukairyuṣmābhirbhavitavyam | upāsakāḥ śarīraṃ yathā jñāsyanti, tathā kariṣyanti | etaddarśayati - yadetaddharmaśarīram, etadyuṣmābhiḥ paripālitavyam | upāsakābahuvyagrāḥ | asamartha dharmadhāraṇaṃ kartum | anena cirasthitenāhaṃ cirasthitiko bhaviṣyāmīti | yathā ca devāvatārasūtre utpalavarṇābhikṣuṇyā cakravartirūpaṃ nirmāya bhagavān devalokāvatīrṇaḥ prathamaṃ vanditaḥ | sā tuṣṭā | mayā bhagavān prathamaṃ vanditaḥ | tasyāśca ( - - - - - - - ) taṃ jñātvā srotāpattiphalaṃ prāptam | etaddarśayati - na mātāpitṛsaṃbhavena śarīreṇa varṇitena vandito bhavāmi | yena phalaṃ prāptaṃ vanditaḥ | etadarthameva ca tatra gāthoktāḥ -
children.translated_text: ) What is to be done after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing): 'You shall honor the <s>Dharma</s>' — this was said. '<s>Tathāgatas</s> have the <s>Dharma</s> as their body (<s>dharmakāya</s>).' In the <s>Mahāparinirvāṇa</s> [sūtra], the noble <s>Ānanda</s> asks: 'How should we [conduct ourselves], O Blessed One, [after your passing]?' The Blessed One said: '<s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> should not be worshipped with garlands, incense, powders, unguents, flower-garlands, or parasols. But whoever, <s>Ānanda</s>, whether monk or nun, layman or laywoman, abides practicing the <s>Dharma</s>, practicing correctly, following the <s>Dharma</s> properly — that one honors the <s>Tathāgata</s>, reveres him, respects him, venerates him, worships him with the supreme worship.' Therefore, the <s>Dharma</s> alone is the body of the Blessed One. Just as in the <s>Karmavibhaṅga</s> [it is said]: 'In relation to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, a mind of faith should be produced.' In the <s>Vinaya</s> [it is said]: '<s>Ānanda</s>, do not grieve, do not lament. Has it not been declared by me before that there is separation and parting from all that is dear and beloved?' And: 'It is impossible, <s>Ānanda</s>, that what is born, become, conditioned, and subject to disintegration should not disintegrate.'

body.translated_text: This the Blessed One demonstrates: just as the <s>Agnihotra</s> is the foremost of all sacrifices that are performed; the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is foremost among the <s>Vedas</s>; among all men the king is foremost; among rivers the ocean is supreme; among stars the moon is chief; among those that shine the sun is preeminent, illuminating a thousand world-systems — so too, whoever reflects 'a gift given to this one person yields great fruit,' the Blessed One says: 'The <s>Sambuddha</s> is the foremost of those worthy of offerings.' For this reason too the Blessed One is foremost. This <s>sūtra</s> should be understood in detail in the <s>Brāhmaṇanipāta</s> section of the <s>Āgama</s>. And as the Blessed One stated previously in the <s>Dakṣiṇāvibhaṅga Sūtra</s>: 'This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the foremost among individual recipients of offerings: namely, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One.' Thus should the supremacy of the Blessed One be declared. And as in the <s>Mahāsamājīya</s>, the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, and other sūtras, there was an assembly of gods from a radius of twelve <s>yojanas</s>. As in the Great Miracle (<s>Mahāprātihārya</s>), he was worshipped by the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> and other gods. And having seen the Great Miracle, many hundreds of non-Buddhist teachers went forth [into the Buddhist order]. And ascetics such as <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> and others went forth. And wanderers such as <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> and others went forth. And <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> such as <s>Brahmāyu</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, and others became devoted. Likewise kings such as <s>Prasenajit</s> and <s>Bimbisāra</s> and others, and householders such as <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> and <s>Ghoṣila</s> and others. Thus those who are foremost among gods and among humans became devoted to the Blessed One. For this reason too the Blessed One is foremost. Moreover, as stated in the <s>Ekottarikāgratāsūtra</s>: 'Endowed with the foremost <s>dharma</s>, he has attained the status of being foremost among gods and humans, rejoicing.' This means: the <s>dharma</s> leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been attained. For that reason he is foremost. What is the reason? Even formerly, when he was still a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, gods approached him — as in the <s>Govindasūtra</s>, in the <s>Śatavarga</s>, and in the <s>Tāpasasūtra</s>, where <s>Indra</s> approached him. At that time he was endowed with the foremost <s>dharma</s>; now the path leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been attained. For that reason he is foremost. Thus too the <s>dharmas</s> have been taught. body.translated_text: For this reason too, the <s>Dharma</s> alone is the body of the Blessed One. Just as in the <s>Bodhimūlasūtra</s>, the Blessed One was dwelling in <s>Ayodhyā</s>. By the time the sick monk recovered and they reached [<s>Ayodhyā</s>], the Blessed One had already attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. The monk was deeply distressed: 'I have not seen the Blessed One!' children.translated_text: ) Thus have they understood. The <s>Buddha</s> has entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Our gods still remain. And so we say: whoever remains and [to whom] devotees offer food, incense, flowers, perfume, lamps, meals, garments, ornaments, silver, or gold — does he not accept it by hand to hand? If he does not accept it, what distinction is there between the <s>Buddha</s> and those [gods]? Now, it is held: either the images of the gods or their replicas are worshipped. We too have the <s>Dharma</s>-body of the <s>Buddha</s> remaining. And the virtues are worshipped. Those who offer incense, perfume, and flowers at images — when this is done, there is merit in what is given at our <s>stūpas</s>. They are worshipped. Since [the <s>Buddha</s>] does not accept it [personally], the gods therefore do not exist. If the gods do exist, why do they not accept [the offerings]? What is the reason? The Blessed One said: 'By the conjunction of three [factors], an offering (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) becomes of great fruit: if there is a giver, if there is the material to be given such as silver and gold, and if there are those worthy of offerings (<s>dakṣiṇīya</s>) — recipients, whether gods or humans.' Thus through the conjunction of these three. It is not that a gift given hand to hand becomes of great fruit. If [the gods] truly exist, why do they not accept [the offerings]? For their devotees! If they do accept, [it is] for their devotees. If they do not accept, why? Now, it would be appropriate if anger were the reason for [the devotees accepting] thus. Now, for those [others]: 'Truly, our god is not angry,' they say. We reply: if they are not angry, why do they not accept? Therefore that [god] does not exist. This is the third reason. And whatever gold or silver the devotees of those gods offer at the feet [of the idols] — what then is the god's connection to it? If that [offering] is used for incense, flowers, perfume, garland-making, or other purposes — then for the one who gave it, there is the fruit of merit. But if that material is taken by others entirely, there is no meritorious fruit for the giver. And those who take it [say]: 'We are devotees of the god, we subsist at the god's feet; the god and we are one.' For them — in the unauthorized appropriation of the god's property — what is the reason? Someone else should take the god's property. Should one equal to the god take the property, or one superior? But no one is equal to the god, let alone more excellent. Are they then more excellent [than the god]? What is the reason? Because they prostrate at his feet and sleep at the god's feet. If they are more excellent, why is the god propitiated? Now, if there is no sin in taking the god's property, then for other thieves too — those who live by theft and who steal others' property — there would also be no sin. Now, [the analogy of] mother, father, son, king, and servant: just as a son takes the father's property by inheritance, or a servant takes the king's property — so too do we. But this too is improper. What is the reason? For a son taking the father's property — there is great sin [if unauthorized]. Now, it is held that it is like the king's servant's property. We reply: a king would punish a son taking what is not given, and a father would give to a son — let alone a servant! Therefore this very illustration applies to us. And as for their understanding — 'We are devotees of the god and subsist at his feet, therefore we take' — that too is improper. What is the reason? Those who are devotees of the god do not take the god's property. If they do take it, they are not devotees. No one who is truly devoted takes the god's property. Their devotion is not to the god; their devotion is to the god's property. For those who take what is not given, there is indeed some sin. What is the reason? As the ancient sages said: 'When the root is cut, [the tree is destroyed]. For one whose paternal affection is destroyed at the root of the austerity-tree, the rest of the people [follow suit].' This means: whoever takes the god's property that has not been given — there is nothing that cannot be done by that person. What is the reason? (
[Reference: KVU, Vaidya 218]

) They are not devotees. But if they are devotees, then who has been declared to be the enemies of the god? Now, if [it is] thought: 'Since they are selfless, their wealth is of no use to them' — it is replied: There is a tradition among some gods that destruction of divine sacrifice and seizure of the earth has been committed. Why are they not selfless? [Response:] Because it was given to us, not to the god. It is replied: For what purpose [was it given] by the patron of the gift? It was given to us alone. Since [you] have abandoned what belongs to the god, therefore it was not given to you. Now, if [it is] thought: 'It is the very satisfaction of the god that we accept it' — for what reason did the god not tell the giver: 'Give to these ones; having been given to them, I shall be pleased'? Since the giver was not instructed by the god, and yet they have taken [the offerings], therefore there is no meritorious fruit for the giver. And for those who take, it is taking what has not been given (<s>adattādāna</s>). Now, if [it is] thought: '[The merit goes to] the god's merit...' — that too is unjustified. For what reason? Because the god did not personally take that wealth with his own hand and place it in their hands. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated: 'By the conjunction of three [factors], the religious gift (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) becomes of great fruit.' Thus, how has [the gift] not been given? And how are these [priests] distinguished from [others]? It is replied: They will even commit the seizure of others' property. And there are some who... live by various [means]. They do not take others' property [only] because they lack the power. Some [refrain] out of fear of punishment by the king. These are the... of the gods, of the devotees of the gods, and of the religious duty of the gods. And even now, this truth should be stated: regarding the god's pilgrimage as well — who receives [the merit of] those [pilgrimages]? And the banks of those rivers are wide... [the sages] have passed away. Those who proclaim at the sacred fords — who receives [the merit of] their pilgrimage? Now, if [it is] thought: 'We bathe in the river aiming at the sacred ford, [because] from this river, from that ford...' — then our position is established. For what reason? The body of our <s>Buddha</s> endures. His virtues are worshipped. And the <s>stūpas</s> receive incense and flowers. [But those] rivers have abandoned their ancient course and flow through different regions of the earth. And those <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) have passed away. Therefore, no one receives [the merit of] their pilgrimage. Of the same kind are the honors and the like offered to the <s>ṛṣis</s>, the <s>Brahmarṣis</s> (Brahmanical sages). For what reason? Some hold the following beliefs: <s>Brahmā</s> is their origin. Some worship [according to] <s>Kāśyapa</s>'s tradition. For some, <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) is the creator. Others say: '<s>Prajāpati</s> (the Lord of Creatures) created the beings. From his mouth [came] the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. From his arms, the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. From his thighs, the <s>Vaiśyas</s>. From his feet, the <s>Śūdras</s>.' Thus they believe. We say: examined from ancient times by the gods, this is the most sinful and not to be listened to. For what reason? Whatever beings there are, two-footed or four-footed — their emergence is from the opening of the womb. What follows [from this]? <s>Prajāpati</s>'s [beings came from] four kinds of birth first — not from four [body] parts. They were created by mental conception alone. And thus... all were born from the mouth alone. How could the four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) be born from a single person? And if the four <s>varṇas</s> were born from <s>Prajāpati</s>, then these classes — <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, <s>Mlecchas</s> (barbarians)... — from where did they appear? Likewise elephants, cattle, horses, and the like. For what reason? Their names are not mentioned here. Why was it not said: 'From the crown of the head... from the soles of the feet, the <s>Mlecchas</s>; women from the back; elephants, cattle, horses, and the like were born from the big toe'? Or else, why was it not said: 'From the head the <s>Asuras</s> were born, from the hands...'? Since the names of these [beings] were not mentioned, therefore the more numerous [creatures] such as animals, birds, and so forth [are unaccounted for]. Since this is contradictory in its earlier and later [parts], and since these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>... are equal — [if we follow the logic:] the first son of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the second a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, the third a <s>Vaiśya</s>, the fourth a <s>Śūdra</s>, and the fifth a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>... then subsequent [sons] would be even lower. For what reason? <s>Prajāpati</s> had four sons. Those [sons] had unlimited sons. Likewise for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>'s and for the <s>Vaiśya</s>'s (

children.translated_text: ) The first son of a <s>Śūdra</s> is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; the second is a <s>Kṣatriya</s>; the third is a <s>Vaiśya</s>; the fourth is a <s>Śūdra</s>; the fifth is a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>; the rest are even lower. For what reason? The fruit resembles the seed. Just as <s>Prajāpati</s> [produced] the four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), so among his sons and lineages there will be four <s>varṇas</s>. Now, if the sons of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are all <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, then they would be more distinguished than <s>Prajāpati</s>. But if they are more distinguished than <s>Prajāpati</s>, what is the purpose [of his creative role]? Or if it is held that <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are lower than <s>Prajāpati</s>, then the first son of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would be a <s>Śūdra</s>, and the rest even lower. Inasmuch as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman, being the daughter of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, if she was born from his mouth, would therefore be [sexually] unapproachable. But if born from [his] feet, she would be a <s>Śūdra</s> woman. Thus there are immeasurable faults in their examination of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Now, if it is held that <s>Prajāpati</s> is the creator, what purpose does <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord God) serve? Or if <s>Īśvara</s> is the creator, for what reason? Since it has been said: 'This world was created by <s>Brahmā</s>, fashioned by <s>Lokeśvara</s> (Lord of the World), made by <s>Prajāpati</s>' — which of these would be true? Thus those <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers), contradicting each other, quarrel. And if it is held that they create beings unitedly — that too is untenable. For what reason? They are like rival border kings, each with their own egoism: 'I am the creator! I am the creator!' As stated —

body.translated_text: Monks: one who is capable, disciplined, confident, learned, a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, one who practices in accordance with the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s> — such a one adorns the <s>Saṅgha</s>. [So too] a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun), an <s>upāsaka</s> (male lay-follower), an <s>upāsikā</s> (female lay-follower). Monks: those who are capable, disciplined, confident, learned, righteous, practicing in accordance with the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s> — they adorn the <s>Saṅgha</s>. That <s>sūtra</s> too should be cited. Moreover, even with regard to a single person who is free from passion (<s>vītarāga</s>), the offering made to us is immeasurable. As stated in the <s>Ugrasūtra</s>: 'See, <s>Ugra</s>! A monk, covered with his robe, dwells having attained immeasurable <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration). The overflow of merit from that merit is immeasurable — an overflow of wholesome [qualities], a nourishment of happiness. Likewise, having partaken of alms-food (<s>piṇḍapāta</s>), lodging (<s>śayanāsana</s>), and medicine for the sick (<s>glānapratyayabhaiṣajya</s>), he dwells having attained immeasurable <s>samādhi</s>. Just as, <s>Ugra</s> householder, many great rivers come together — their water cannot be counted — and yet they are reckoned as an immeasurable, incalculable, great mass of water. Which great rivers? The <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Sarayū</s>, <s>Āryavatī</s>, and <s>Mahī</s>. Their water cannot be counted, yet they are reckoned as an immeasurable, incalculable, great mass of water. Even so, <s>Ugra</s>: see, a monk, using his robe, dwells having attained immeasurable <s>samādhi</s>. Likewise, using alms-food, lodging, and medicine for the sick, he dwells having attained immeasurable <s>samādhi</s>. The overflow of merit from that merit is immeasurable — an overflow of wholesome [qualities], a nourishment of happiness.' Thus, even what is given to a single virtuous person among us bears immeasurable fruit. Likewise [with] the giving of parks (<s>ārāmadāna</s>) and monasteries (<s>vihāradāna</s>). The details should be understood from the <s>Velāmasūtra</s> and the <s>Dakṣiṇāsūtra</s>. And likewise, the fruit of worship performed at the <s>stūpa</s> of the Blessed One who has entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is immeasurable. As stated in the <s>Karmavibhaṅga</s>: 'There are ten benefits of worshipping the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' What is the reason? Whatever donor gives a gift — whether desiring great wealth, or contemplating heavenly happiness, or for the sake of liberation — all that has been declared: that one becomes greatly wealthy, is reborn in the heavens, and quickly attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Thus the fruit for one who has done service at a <s>stūpa</s> is immeasurable — not like the words of others whom <s>Devadatta</s> takes hold of. There is a <s>karma</s> according to our [teaching]: whoever steals what has been given at a <s>stūpa</s> — the sin thereof is immeasurable. For those [sins], comparisons do not serve as a measure. Whatever gold, silver, wealth, grain, garments, ornaments, and the like belong to all beings on this earth — whoever commits theft of all that — the sin of one who steals what has been given at a <s>stūpa</s> is even more abundant than that sin. This is our established doctrine: what is given at a <s>stūpa</s> should be used for the <s>stūpa</s> alone; what is [given] to the <s>Saṅgha</s> should be used for the <s>Saṅgha</s> alone. This established doctrine has been set forth. Just as our Blessed One endures, so too the service done to him bears immeasurable fruit. But how much merit accrues from offerings made to those external gods?

body.text: evaṃ te sahitā bhūtvā asamarthāḥ prajānirmāṇe | evaṃ teṣāṃ mātāpi | mahādoṣaḥ karmaṇā na kiṃcinmātraiva pradarśitam | atha matam - adyāpi sāvakāśam, yasmānnāmagrahaṇaṃ na kṛtam | ucyate | adya niravakāśaṃ yasmānnāmagrahaṇaṃ na kṛtam | kiṃ kāraṇam? ekasya doṣe datte śeṣā doṣā bhavanti | etaduktaṃ bhavati - yadi tava brāhmaṇārthaṃ saha kathāṃ kuryāt, sa tasya doṣo dātavyaḥ | yadi kṣatriyeṇa, yadi vaiśyena, yadi śūdreṇa saha kathā kriyate, yadevamāsṛtya śūdraḥ kathāṃ kuryāt saha vaktavyam | tasmādayaṃ doṣaḥ ityevaṃ niravakāśaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati | ya evaṃ pratipannāḥ - buddhaḥ parinirvṛtaḥ, kastāḥ pūjāḥ parigṛhṇātīti, teṣāmeva svasiddhāntadoṣo vaktavyaḥ | tasmātteṣāmeva pratisvaṃ svasiddhāntānāṃ doṣo dātavyaḥ | kiṃ kāraṇam? na hyabhiyuktasya paścātpratyabhiyogaḥ | tasmādanekaprakāreṇa teṣāṃ pūrvābhiyogaḥ kārya iti | na caitadanarthamuktam | atraikottarikāsūtraṃ pratyavagantavyam - trīṇīmāni bhikṣavaḥ pracchannavāhīnīti | katamāni trīṇi? mātṛgrāmaḥ kūṭakārṣāpaṇo brāhmaṇānāṃ siddhāntaḥ | trīṇīmāni bhikṣavaḥ vivṛtāni śobhanti iti | katamāni trīṇi? candramaṇḍalaṃ sūryamaṇḍalaṃ buddhavacanam | imāni trīṇi vivṛtāni śobhanti | yānyetāni parīkṣākāraṇāni devapūjāprajāpatiprabhṛtīnāṃ sadā kāryamadhikṛtya bhagavatoktam - brāhmaṇānāṃ siddhāntaḥ pracchannavāhī | mahākarmavibhaṅga ucyate - mahānti karmāṇi | atra vistareṇa vibhaktāni | tasmānmahākarmavibhaṅgaḥ | saṃgrahasārakarmavibhaṅgasarvasārakarmaṇāṃ hīnotkṛṣṭamadhyamāni vistareṇa kathāmukhāni darśitāni | tasmādapi mahākarmavibhaṅgaḥ gotrāntarīyāṇāmabhidharmasaṃyukteṣu ||
body.translated_text: Thus, even united, they are incapable of creating beings. Likewise, their [doctrines about their own] mother [suffer from] great faults — through <s>karma</s>, not even the slightest has been demonstrated [correctly]. Now, if it is held that 'there is still room [for argument], since [specific] names have not been mentioned' — we reply: now there is no room, precisely because names have not been mentioned. For what reason? When a fault is given to one [doctrine], the remaining faults follow. This amounts to saying: if one were to hold a conversation with you for the sake of [refuting] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [doctrines], that fault must be given to him; and if the conversation is with a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a <s>Vaiśya</s>, or a <s>Śūdra</s>, then whatever doctrine the <s>Śūdra</s> relies upon, a conversation should be held with him, saying 'therefore this is the fault' — thus it is made impossible to escape. Those who hold that 'the <s>Buddha</s> has entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — who accepts those offerings?' — to them, the fault in their own established doctrines should be pointed out. Therefore, the fault in each of their respective doctrines should be given to them. For what reason? A counter-charge cannot be brought against the original accuser. Therefore, in many ways, a prior charge should first be brought against them. And this has not been said to no purpose. Here the <s>Ekottarikā Sūtra</s> should be understood: 'Monks, these three things flow in concealment.' What three? Womankind, counterfeit coinage, and the doctrines of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. 'Monks, these three things shine when revealed.' What three? The disc of the moon, the disc of the sun, and the word of the <s>Buddha</s>. These three things shine when revealed. Regarding these examinations concerning the worship of gods, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the rest — the Blessed One has stated, with reference to this very matter: 'The doctrines of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> flow in concealment.' This is called the <s>Mahākarmavibhaṅga</s> (Great Classification of Karma) because: great are the <s>karmas</s> (actions); here they have been classified in detail. Therefore it is the <s>Mahākarmavibhaṅga</s>. The essential <s>karmavibhaṅga</s>, summarizing all essential karmas — inferior, superior, and middling — has been shown in detail through narrative topics. Therefore too it is the <s>Mahākarmavibhaṅga</s>. [It also concerns] those of other lineages, in connection with the <s>Abhidharma</s>.
Thus the <s>Mahākarmavibhaṅga</s> (Great Classification of Karma) is completed.
